text: [image: Before and after, by group: the share likely to vote for Jonny Larsen before and after reading his bio. Everyone, 45.8% to 59.5% (+13.7). Republicans, 35.9% to 51.2% (+15.3). Unaffiliated voters, 53.9% to 68.6% (+14.7). Undecided voters, 14.1% to 47.3% (+33.2). Rep. Kennedy voters, 7.0% to 20.7% (+13.7).]

[image: Getting to know Jonny Larsen: voters who know him favor him 3 to 1. Half of respondents have heard of him: 22.9% favorable, 7.2% unfavorable, 19.9% no opinion. The other 50.0% had not heard of him. After reading his bio, 59.5% of all respondents were likely to vote for him.]
[image: Jonny Larsen’s statement about the internal survey, the same text as on this page, with notes on how the survey was conducted.]

[image: Rep. Kennedy’s record: more than 6 in 10 are dissatisfied with Rep. Kennedy. Completely satisfied 10.2%, somewhat satisfied 26.0%, somewhat dissatisfied 21.7%, completely dissatisfied 42.1%. Satisfied 36.2%, dissatisfied 63.8%.]

[image: The Utah Debate Commission’s poll as published on Sept. 24, 2026: 513 respondents, margin of error ±4.32%. Mike Kennedy 41.7%, Jonny Larsen 32.9%, Steven Burt 5.7%, Taylor Wright 5.3%, other 2.5%, undecided 11.9%.]

[image: The ballot: Jonny Larsen leads Rep. Kennedy by 23 points. Asked who they would vote for if the election for Congress were held today: Jonny Larsen 47.7%, Mike Kennedy 25.0%, other 3.7%, undecided 23.6%.]

[image: Utah Debate Commission poll: nearly 6 in 10 respondents did not pick Rep. Kennedy. Mike Kennedy 41.7%, Jonny Larsen 32.9%, Steven Burt 5.7%, Taylor Wright 5.3%, other 2.5%, undecided 11.9%. In 2018, Ben McAdams trailed Rep. Mia Love by 9.2 points in the same poll, then won the seat. Jonny Larsen trails Rep. Kennedy by 8.8.]

[image: What matters most: the economy and cost of living matter most to nearly 9 in 10 voters. Then government corruption and accountability, more than 6 in 10; Utah’s land, water and environment, more than half; healthcare costs and access, about 1 in 3; immigration and the border, about 1 in 4.]

[image: When voters meet Jonny Larsen: his story moved voters 13.7 points. Likely to vote for him before reading his bio: 45.8% likely, 29.2% unsure, 25.0% unlikely. After: 59.5% likely, 20.9% unsure, 19.6% unlikely. His bio moved nearly half of unsure voters, and 1 in 5 unlikely voters, to likely.]

[image: Who we heard from: 56% are registered Republicans. Party registration on the voter file for the 1,270 respondents: Republican 56.1%, Democratic 12.9%, unaffiliated 24.1%, other 6.9%. The district: 55.7%, 10.5%, 27.9% and 5.9%.]
